output.summary: An annual pulse native to the northeastern Mediterranean, white lupin occurs naturally from the Balkans to Sicily and Turkey. It has winter and spring forms. Its seeds are eaten as snacks, commonly after soaking or brining, and in parts of Greece after brief seawater soaking before being consumed raw.
output.edibilityNote: Seeds are eaten as snacks, usually soaked or brined; in parts of Greece they are briefly seawater-soaked and eaten raw.
